title: Section-normalized ordinary evaluation and its inverse pullback mate
statement:
Let $C_n$ be commutative rings with arbitrary inverse transition homomorphisms, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a scheme morphism. On the small pro-etale sites let $\mathscr S_T$ be the strict semilinear module-system category and $\mathcal T_T(C_n)=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N^{op},\operatorname{Mod}(\underline{C_n}_T))$ the constant-coefficient strict-tower category, with the specified ordinary adjunctions of [def-sp-semilinear-constant-ring-operations]. Write $e_{n,T}:\mathscr S_T\to\operatorname{Mod}(\underline{C_n}_T)$ for evaluation, $\Delta_T$ for the constant-diagram functor, and $E^0_{n,T}=\Delta_Te_{n,T}$. There is a unique isomorphism
$$D_{f,n}:E^0_{n,Y}f_{*,\bullet}\xrightarrow{\sim}f_{*,n}^{\mathcal T}E^0_{n,X}$$
whose component at every tower index $m$, section object $H$ and system $M$ is the identity on $M_n(H\times_YX)$. Its inverse has the same normalization. The inverse adjunction mate
$$a_{f,n}:f_n^{*,\mathcal T}E^0_{n,Y}\longrightarrow E^0_{n,X}f_\bullet^*$$
of $D_{f,n}$ is invertible. More precisely it is the constant-diagram lift, with the canonical constant-diagram compositors, of the single-level inverse-image evaluation comparison uniquely fixed by the unit equation. If $\eta_f$ and $\eta_f^{\mathcal T}$ are the specified ordinary units, this equation is
$$f_{*,n}^{\mathcal T}(a_{f,n,M})\circ\eta^{\mathcal T}_{f,E^0_{n,Y}M}=D_{f,n,f_\bullet^*M}\circ E^0_{n,Y}(\eta_{f,M}).$$
The comparisons consequently identify the specified counits as well. They are natural transformations on the entire ordinary system category, for arbitrary coefficient transitions.

proof.text: Take the normalized single-level comparison d from evaluationPush_existsUnique in [lem-sf-semilinear-evaluation-ring-square]. Lift its components to constant diagrams, using the termwise tower direct image of [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations], to obtain D. Both directions retain their identity-on-sections normalization. Extensionality on sections, tower components and natural-transformation components proves uniqueness of D. The same normalization and evalPushOrdinary_existsUnique identify its chosen comparison with D inverse.

Unfold the specified evalPullInv of [def-sp-semilinear-constant-ring-operations] and substitute the chosen comparison identified in Step 1. This is exactly the inverse mate of D hom. Apply the already proved evalPullInv_isIso, owned by the same definition node: its existing proof constructs the single-level inverse-image comparison and lifts the unit-normalized mate to constant diagrams. Thus invertibility is reused from a complete proof, not inferred from invertibility of D. Apply unit_mateEquiv_symm of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] to obtain the stated tower unit equation.

Evaluate the isomorphism asIso(evalPullInv) at tower index zero, obtaining the actual level isomorphism b. Evaluate the tower unit equation at zero to obtain its level unit equation. Naturality of evalPullInv along the opposite of 0 <= m identifies its component at m with that at zero: source and target towers are constant, so both structure maps are identities. To prove uniqueness, apply injectivity of the level adjunction Hom equivalence to each component of any proposed b. Its Hom image is the level unit followed by direct image of b; the two unit equations therefore identify these images. Isomorphism and natural-transformation extensionality finish. This also proves that every normalized b agrees with all tower components.

Apply mateEquiv_counit_symm of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] to D hom and reverse the equality. Substituting the inverse-mate identity from Step 2 yields exactly the required counit equation for the specified adjunctions. No coefficient, transition or morphism restrictions were introduced.
